title: That 'Buy Now' Button Cost You $1,300 by Design
hook: Amazon patented one-click ordering in 1999 and defended it in court for 20 years — every checkout step they strip away makes you spend 12 percent more, adding up to $1,300 a year.
angle: Not just 'impulse buying is bad' — the specific engineering of checkout friction removal, documented spending increases per step removed, and deliberate UI design choices that extract money
audience: Anyone who shops online or uses delivery apps — basically every adult under 60
key_numbers: 12% more spent per checkout step removed
35% higher checkout completion from large confirm buttons
246 impulse digital purchases per year (avg American)
68% of subscribers pay 3 months longer when cancellation is hard
